meter.title: Grid meter
meter.description: These grid meters were found. A meter read directly gives a value about every second (read-only, nothing on the meter changes); a meter of another integration uses its sensors. Or choose the phases and sensors yourself. HomeBatteryAssist only reads the meter.

direct.title: Meter read directly
direct.description: Choose the type of meter and enter its IP address. HomeBatteryAssist reads it about every second, read-only; nothing on the meter changes. For an SMA Home Manager / Energy Meter enter the address it sends from.

user.title: Grid connection
user.description: Is your home connected to the grid with 1 phase or 3 phases?

max_current.title: Connection size
max_current.description: Select the size of your grid connection (main fuse rating per phase). You can find it on your energy contract or on the main fuse in your meter cupboard.

sensors.title: Phase measurements
sensors.description: Select for each phase the sensor that measures the power (W) or current (A) on that phase, typically from your smart meter (P1). If this sensor is positive for import and negative for export, leave the return sensor empty. If your meter has separate sensors for import and export (return), select both. Note: current sensors usually cannot tell import from export.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: HomeBatteryAssist records your house consumption to predict future usage, and plans ahead using price and PV forecasts from other integrations. The system plans at most the chosen number of days ahead, and never further than the price and PV forecasts reach.

data_description.history_interval: A shorter interval is more precise but stores more data.
data_description.planning_horizon_days: How many days ahead the system may plan at most.
data_description.price_forecast_entity: Sensor of an energy price integration (e.g. Nordpool, ENTSO-e, Frank Energie) whose attributes contain the upcoming prices.
data_description.pv_forecast_entries: Integrations providing a solar forecast (e.g. Forecast.Solar, Solcast). Selected forecasts are added up to the total for your home.
data_description.forecast_interval: How often the forecasts are recalculated automatically.
data_description.plan_mode: How HomeBatteryAssist would control the batteries (advice only for now). Both modes are always calculated for comparison.
data_description.export_price_factor: Used with 'Import price x factor', and wherever the export price sensors give no price.
data_description.cycle_cost: Cost per kWh through the battery (wear), in the price unit; avoids charging/discharging for tiny gains.
data_description.min_battery_power: Below this power the conversion losses of a battery are high: a request is spread over as few batteries as possible, each running at least at this power, and over more batteries when more power is needed.
data_description.balance_interval: How often to check whether another battery should take over, so the batteries stay equally full. In between, the batteries in use are kept.
data_description.full_charge_window_days: When a battery has not been fully charged within its interval, a full charge is forced at the cheapest moment within this many days before the deadline.
data_description.phase_margin: Part of the main fuse rating that the batteries always leave free on every phase (the same for all phases). With 3x25A and 10% the batteries keep each phase below 22.5 A, in the plan and in the simulation.
data_description.export_price_mode: What energy returned to the grid earns. Import price x factor (below), the bare market price (EPEX, from the selected sensors, or from market attributes of the price sensor), or an export price forecast from the selected sensors. Where these do not reach, import price x factor is used.
data_description.export_price_entities: One or more sensors with prices (state and/or price list attributes), e.g. a market price sensor for today/tomorrow plus a forecast sensor for the days after. For overlapping periods the first sensor wins.
data_description.max_cycles_per_day: Arbitrage charges and discharges at most this many full cycles per day (energy discharged / capacity), to spare the batteries. 0 = no limit.
data_description.pv_forecast_margin: The plans count on this much less solar power than forecast, to hedge optimistic forecasts: more is charged from the grid where needed. Comes on top of the correction learned from past forecasts.
data_description.peak_limit_w: Peak shaving on the total grid import (all phases together): the arbitrage plans keep energy in reserve to stay below this power, and virtual batteries take load off when it is exceeded. Next to the per-phase protection of the main fuse. 0 = off.

error.duplicate_sensor: Each phase needs its own sensor.

abort.single_instance_allowed: HomeBatteryAssist is already configured. Only one instance is allowed.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The grid connection has been changed.

recalculate.name: Recalculate
recalculate.description: Recalculates the forecasts of HomeBatteryAssist now, e.g. when new prices or PV forecasts arrive. Only HomeBatteryAssist's own forecasts are recalculated; no device is controlled.

import_history.name: Import consumption history
import_history.description: Fills the consumption history from Home Assistant's statistics, e.g. as starting data for forecasts. By default the house consumption is reconstructed from the configured sensors (grid, PV, excluded devices, batteries). Own measurements are never overwritten unless Replace is on.

days.name: Days
days.description: How many days back to import (at most the retention of 28 days).

source_entity.name: Consumption sensor (optional)
source_entity.description: Take over the house consumption of this sensor instead of reconstructing it, e.g. from Omnibattery.

battery_power_history.name: Older battery power sensors (optional)
battery_power_history.description: Earlier power sensors of the battery (same direction), used for the period before its current sensor existed.

replace.name: Replace own measurements
replace.description: Let imported values replace own measurements in the same periods.

adjust_forecast.name: Adjust consumption forecast
adjust_forecast.description: Changes the expected house consumption for a period, e.g. from a script for a holiday, guests or a planned large load. Give a start (default: now), an end or duration, and exactly one change: a factor, an offset in W or a fixed power in W. Adjustments are kept until their end.

name.name: Name
name.description: Shown in the forecast and the decision log, and usable to remove it again.

end.name: End
end.description: End of the period (or give a duration).

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Length of the period (instead of an end).

factor.name: Factor
factor.description: Multiply the expected consumption, e.g. 0.3 while on holiday or 1.5 with guests.

offset_w.name: Extra power
offset_w.description: Add (or with a minus subtract) this power in W, e.g. 2000 for the oven.

power_w.name: Fixed power
power_w.description: Replace the expected consumption by this power in W.

clear_forecast_adjustments.name: Remove forecast adjustments
clear_forecast_adjustments.description: Removes adjustments of the consumption forecast by id or name; without id or name all adjustments are removed.

id.name: Id
id.description: Id(s) of the adjustments to remove.

name.name: Name
name.description: Name(s) of the adjustments to remove.

set_forecast_correction.name: Set forecast correction
set_forecast_correction.description: Controls how a forecast is corrected from its running accuracy: learned (default), off (only measure) or manual with an own value. Optionally for one lead time and for a limited time.

kind.name: Forecast
kind.description: Which forecast: consumption, PV, price or all.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: learned: use the running accuracy; off: do not correct; manual: use the given value.

value.name: Value
value.description: Manual correction: a factor for PV (e.g. 0.85), an offset in W for consumption, an offset in the price unit for prices.

bucket.name: Lead time
bucket.description: Only for predictions made this long before the period (default: all).

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Return to learned after this time (default: until changed).

reset_forecast_accuracy.name: Reset forecast accuracy
reset_forecast_accuracy.description: Forgets what was learned about a forecast (e.g. after switching PV forecast provider) and starts measuring again.

kind.name: Forecast
kind.description: Which forecast: consumption, PV, price or all.

set_plan_mode.name: Set battery plan mode
set_plan_mode.description: Chooses the mode of the battery plan (advice): zero on the meter or arbitrage.

end_before_start.message: The end of the adjustment must be after its start.

manual_needs_value.message: A manual correction needs a value.

import_direct_meter.message: The grid meter is read directly, so Home Assistant has no history of it. Choose a sensor with the house consumption to take over (source_entity).
